A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same VEGA-3D work, with matching method equations, figures and benchmark tables supporting reliable comparison. v1 includes supplementary Sections A–F; the supplied v2 ends after the references. This omission is a document difference, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-understanding, spatial-reasoning and simulated-manipulation results, alongside backbone/fusion ablations, efficiency measurements and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and adds a real-robot Click Bell evaluation reporting success counts for VEGA-3D and a baseline policy.

M1.justification: The frozen video-diffusion feature extractor, noise injection, intermediate-layer extraction and adaptive gated fusion remain unchanged in Sections 3–4. v2 clarifies the existing VLA integration; neither this clarification nor omission of the supplementary training pseudocode establishes a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 extends evaluation beyond simulated manipulation to physical Agilex Piper arms on the RoboTwin Click Bell task. This introduces a materially different deployment environment, although coverage is limited to one real-robot task. The five scene-understanding benchmarks, VSI-Bench and four LIBERO suites remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons with Ross3D and Omni-View. Ross3D was previously discussed but had no result row there. Comparator membership in the retained VSI-Bench, LIBERO, backbone and fusion tables is unchanged, making this a focused expansion.

E3.justification: The new Click Bell experiment introduces a RoboTwin-based physical-robot evaluation with 20 trials per policy and success-rate reporting. Existing benchmark settings, including 32 sampled frames, timestep 300, layer 20 and batch size 128, remain unchanged. Missing supplementary settings do not establish changes to those experiments.

E4.justification: v2 omits the SEVA/Vmem timestep sensitivity studies in Table A4 and the ScanRefer success/failure and VSI-Bench case studies in Figures 8–12. Tables A3 and A5 also supplied multi-metric ablation evidence beyond the ScanRefer curve retained in Figure 6. Main backbone, fusion and Wan2.1 noise/depth analyses remain, but supplementary diagnostic coverage is substantially reduced.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C.1 specifies calculating correspondence-score means and standard deviations over valid scenes; this statistical aggregation/reporting description is absent from v2. Neither version provides training-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new robot trial counts describe evaluation sample size, not repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Retained VEGA-3D benchmark scores are unchanged. Table 1 adds Ross3D/Omni-View results and recomputes average ranks, including VEGA-3D's 1.8 to 2.2 under the expanded comparator set. v2 newly reports Click Bell success of 55% (11/20) versus 40% (8/20). It also loses substantial appendix-only results, including SEVA/Vmem sweeps, unplotted ablation metrics and qualitative success/failure outcomes.

T1.justification: Main Equations 1–8 are unchanged. v2 omits Appendix C's explicit definitions of within-view voxel prototypes, correspondence aggregation and separate model-group normalization for NOS. This reduces formal specification, particularly the normalization population, without establishing a changed underlying computation or adding new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and main conclusion retain the same claims: transferable geometric priors from video generators, adaptive fusion with semantic features, and benefits across scene understanding, spatial reasoning and manipulation. The new experiment supports existing claims rather than redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a World-Action Models interpretation and explicitly acknowledges Ross3D's stronger QA scores while emphasizing VEGA-3D's grounding performance. Omission of Appendices E–F removes qualifications about fine-grained instance confusion, manually chosen extraction settings and indoor-centered validation. Existing captioning-tradeoff and inference-cost discussions remain.

D1.justification: v2 loses Algorithm 1, detailed training-data mixtures, per-backbone resolutions/tokenization and feature stages, and correspondence preprocessing details, including depth handling and coordinate alignment. These were substantial reproduction specifications in Appendices A–C. Brief additions identify robot hardware/protocol and clarify VLA integration; the main hyperparameters and code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces a broad contrast with generation/control work by explicit positioning against Ross3D, Omni-View, MILO, GaussianDWM, DyVA and JEPA-VLA. It emphasizes frozen feature extraction relative to auxiliary generation, geometric supervision and predictive world-model approaches. This substantially develops the closest-prior-work discussion; twelve cited works are added.

P1.justification: The organized technical, implementation, scoring, probing, qualitative-results and limitations supplement disappears entirely. v2 also rewrites the video-generation related-work and manipulation discussions, adds World-Action Models and real-robot paragraphs, and adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author information. The principal main-text section sequence remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 omits supplementary Tables A1–A5, Figures 8–12 and the Algorithm 1 display. Table 1 gains two comparator rows, supervision markers and an expanded caption; Table 2 explicitly identifies its baseline. Main Figures 1–7 are retained, with several displays relocated through text reflow rather than replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 improves comparison with close prior work and adds a useful, limited real-robot experiment. These gains do not compensate for losing Appendices A–F: the training pipeline, backbone configurations, precise scoring details, additional sensitivity results and documented failure/applicability limits are no longer supplied. Their omission substantially weakens reproducibility and scrutiny of the central evidence, while the retained benchmark performance is unchanged.
